newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian roasters finding it easier to buy coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian roasters finding it easier to buy coffee.

text.p: Brazilian domestic coffee roasters are finding it easier to buy the coffees they want in the quantity they want as supply from the harvest is picking up, the Sao Paulo State Coffee Industry Union said.
An indicator drawn up by the union fell to 3.95 points in the period of July 7-11 compared with 4.40 and 4.87 points the previous two weeks.
The indicator on a scale of 1 to 9 measures internal supply, with one to three representing normal availability.
The greater supply was also confirmed by the rise in cooperative stocks which increased 27.5 percent at the end of June compared with May, said union president Nathan Herszkowicz.

"This shows that coffees from the current harvest are coming more regularly into the market and that the use of older coffees from public stocks is important at the moment so that roasters can make up their blends," he said.

The union expects to see good demand at the government's auction on July 16 of 149,705 60-kg bags of stocks, particularly given it is the first sale since the National Monetary Council approved an extension in payment terms to 120 days.
